rows.row: BUILD-FAILED: operation 'Fontc' ... FEA parsing failed with 2 errors
rows.cause: Cardo-Regular-TTF.sfd names a glyph `10192.04` (gid 3416, Encoding 62520 = U+F438, a salt alternate listed in the AlternateSubs2 of u10192 and u10198). FontForge never goes through FEA, so it exported it (the release post table still names U+F438 `10192.04`). babelfont writes the lookups as FEA, and the OpenType Feature File spec (2.f.i) says a glyph name must not start with a digit. fea-rs rejects both references: 'Unexpected token, expected glyph or glyph class' at `sub u10192 from [Sigma Sigma.09 u10192.03 10192.04];` and `sub u10198 from [u10198.01 10192.04 ...];`. This is not a fontc bug: fontTools feaLib rejects the same FEA. It is a source name that FEA cannot express. Closed by the documented .sfd rename below. The new name is a choice, not a fidelity value, which is why this row is classed as a decision.
rows.evidence: Full diagnostic from fontc (fontc-worktrees/survey-rebase debug build; gftools-builder3 e851b8b with fontc 1.0.0 shows only the count). Minimal repro: investigations/next-cardo/probes/fea_digit_glyphname/{make.py,run.sh,EXPECTED.txt}. DigitName fails in fontc 1.0.0 (builder3 e851b8b) and in feaLib ('Expected glyph name ... found 10192.04'); LetterName (u10192.04) builds in both. After the rename (runs/r1-regular-rename) the style builds and the shared gate shows 1 row.

rows.cause: FontForge tottf.c, unchanged from tag v20110222 to 20170731, sets dirhint = 0 when the exported glyphs include both left-to-right and right-to-left characters (-2 when only RTL, else 2) and sets head.flags bit 9 when it sees RTL. Commit 722e7ea8873e (2017-12-23, 'Skip Apple head table fields in OpenType mode', first in release 20190317) makes OpenType mode write 2 unconditionally. The release was exported by FontForge build 2011-02-22 (FFTM stamp) and Cardo maps Hebrew plus Latin, so it gets 0. fontc 1.0.0 always writes 2: write-fonts Head::default has font_direction_hint 2, fontbe head.rs never overrides it, and FEA can set only FontRevision in the head table (fea-rs HeadBuilder). No Glyphs or FEA source can express the value. The OpenType spec deprecates the field ('Set to 2'), and neither harfrust 0.6.2 nor skrifa 0.47.0 reads it. The row is functionally empty.
rows.evidence: FontForge sources fetched for tags v20110222, v20120731-b, 20141230, 20150824, 20161012, 20170731, 20190317, 20190413, 20190801 and 20230101; the commit list for tottf.c between 2017-07-31 and 2019-08 names 722e7ea8873e. probes/dirhint_oracle.py (runs/dirhint_oracle.txt) computes the pre-722e7ea rule from each release's cmap and matches 147 of 149 releases in both batches. The 2 misses are Tuffy-Regular and Tuffy-Italic, which have no FFTM table and ship 2. All 3 Cardo styles and both Thabit styles have 0, MATCH, bit9=1, FFTM 2011-02-22 or 2008-08-08. probes/table_gate_proposed.py reclassifies this row as RELEASE-STALE in Cardo x3 and Thabit x2 (runs/dirhint_thabit_proposed.txt).

rows.row: hmtx.uni0304 {width:[1000,0]} and hmtx.uni05B105BD {width:[1300,0]} (hidden by the shared gate)
rows.cause: Both glyphs are GlyphClass 4 (mark) with an attach anchor and a non-zero advance (Width 1000 and 1300), and FontForge exported those advances. babelfont's SFD reader gives every GlyphClass-4 glyph subCategory Nonspacing, and --set-subcategory sets Nonspacing again on any mark with an _anchor. glyphs2fontir 1.0.0 then exports a Nonspacing mark at zero width (source.rs:1828). The shared gate never reported the difference: diffenator3 replaced the hmtx section with 'There are 240 changes, check manually!', and table_gate.expand_overflow recomputes only left side bearings.
rows.evidence: probes/advance_audit.py (runs/advance_audit_cardo_r0r1.txt): uni0304 1000 vs 0 and uni05B105BD 1300 vs 0 are HIDDEN in r1. The prototype (reader plus set-subcategory emit 'Spacing Combining' for an advancing mark) gives 0 advance differences in runs/p2-proto/advance_audit.txt, and the proposed gate goes from 2 rows to 0.

rows.row: GPOS mark attachment lost; the gate waved it through as 'legacy kern modernised' (not a blocking row)
rows.cause: babelfont's FontForge reader (upstream commit 66334a7) starts the abvm/blwm/kern/dist/mark/mkmk feature blocks it writes with '# Automatic code start'. fea-rs has_insert_marker and ufo2ft match only '# Automatic Code', case-sensitively. fontc therefore treats the mark feature as hand-written and skips its mark writer: 'Skipping generating feature mark, which is manually declared in FEA and has no insertion comment'. No MarkBasePos lookup is built from the 12 Anchor-N classes. kern is not affected: glyphs-reader appends '# Automatic Code' to any manual kern feature.
rows.evidence: fontc warning reproduced with builder3 e851b8b. probes/shaping_compare.py on runs/r1-regular-rename: 4361 of 181328 base+mark strings and all 45 diffenator3 Hebrew words differ. With the prototype marker fix (runs/p1-proto) 956 base+mark strings and 7 words still differ. probes/automatic_code_marker.py (runs/automatic_code_marker.txt): only Cardo-Regular (mark) and Lohit-Bengali (abvm) lose a writer in the next batch, and no landed repository does.

rows.row: GPOS: marks attached to glyphs made of references (not a gate row)
rows.cause: fontc propagates anchors from components as Glyphs.app does. FontForge exports only a glyph's own anchors, so 1680 reference-only glyphs such as igrave became bases the release never had. The next-provenance unit's filter --fontforge-no-anchor-propagation (Glyphs 'Propagate Anchors' = 0) removes this.
rows.evidence: Stage p1 (marker fix only) vs p2 (plus --fontforge-no-anchor-propagation): base+mark differences go from 956 to 10 of 181328 (runs/shaping_summary.txt). Example in p1: U+00EC U+0300, where the release leaves the mark unattached and ours attaches it.

rows.row: GPOS lookup order: 10 base+mark strings and 7 diffenator3 words, Hebrew cantillation over vowel points (not a gate row)
rows.cause: The release applies FontForge's lookups in .sfd order, which interleaves the mark-to-base lookups (0,1,2,5,6,7,9,10,14,21) with the pair and contextual lookups of the same mark feature. fea-rs inserts generated lookups at next_gpos_id() at the marker (compile_ctx.rs). babelfont defines every FontForge lookup in featurePrefixes, so all 12 generated MarkBasePos lookups come after them (our lookups 20-31).
rows.evidence: probes/lookup_order_test.py: reordering the RELEASE's GPOS the way fontc orders ours makes it equal to our build on all 17 strings. Putting its MarkBasePos lookups FIRST instead leaves the release unchanged on all 241128 base+mark strings and the 17 strings (runs/p2-proto/Cardo-Regular.lookup-order-test*.txt). probes/mark_lookups_after_marker.py moves the 12 lookups that the kern and mark features own after their marker in the .glyphs, and a real builder3 e851b8b build of that file gives 0/181328 base+mark, 0/41683 pairs, 0/15 kern+mark and 0 d3 words, with proposed gate 0 (runs/p3-marks-first).

rows.cause: The .sfd states nonbreakingspace Width 550 and space Width 575. google/fonts d70318ab8 (Dave Crossland, 2015-04-27, 'Updating ofl/cardo/*ttf with nbspace and fsType fixes') edited only Cardo-Italic.ttf. In that binary it changed only the nonbreakingspace advance, 550 to 575 (the space's), plus the cmap re-packing (mappings equal) and the head checksum. fsType was already 0 before and after.
rows.evidence: probes/cardo_release_history.py (runs/cardo_release_history.txt): 90abd17b4 to d70318ab8 changes tables [cmap, head, hmtx], advances [(nonbreakingspace, 550, 575)], cmap mappings equal: True. Regular and Bold binaries are unchanged since 90abd17b4. Edit `nbspwidth` verified in runs/s1-italic-nbsp: the row closes and 10 shared rows become 6.

rows.cause: Only the lookup order differs: babelfont defines 'Single Substitution lookup 9' (longs->s, in no feature and called only by the hist contextual lookup) before the chain that calls it, so every later index shifts by one. Feature membership and rules are equal. arbitrate_gsub_lookup_order refused only because its shaping corpus met the nbsp advance difference ('  ': release 575, ours 550).
rows.evidence: GATE_TRACE=1 on r0: 'shaping differs lang=None word=\' \\xa0\''. After the nbspwidth edit (runs/s1-italic-nbsp) the gate prints 'RELEASE-STALE the same GSUB lookups in a different order; 69696 shaped runs identical across 8 language(s), with the features firing'.

rows.row: hmtx.uni1DC1 [30,0], hmtx.uni2E0F [2443,0], hmtx.uni2E10 [2443,0], hmtx.uni05B105BD [1300,0], plus hidden hmtx.uni2E11 [2443,0] and hmtx.uniF15B [11,0]
rows.cause: All 6 are GlyphClass 4 with a non-zero Width, and the release keeps both GDEF class 3 and the advance. The babelfont SFD reader writes subCategory Nonspacing, and fontc zeroes a Nonspacing mark. uni2E11 and uniF15B were hidden by table_gate.arbitrate_lsb: it marks a whole hmtx row RELEASE-STALE when the release's bearing is stale, even when the row also carries a width difference. Its '"advance" not in row' guard looks for a key diffenator3 never writes; the key is 'width'.
rows.evidence: probes/advance_audit.py lists them as HIDDEN (lsb-arbitration). With the prototype (runs/p2-proto) there are 0 advance differences, and the 6 glyphs are width 30/2443/2443/2443/11/1300 with GDEF class 3 in both fonts.

rows.cause: The .sfd states 15 LCarets2 records (with LigCaretCntFixed: 1), and FontForge's GDEF writer exported them (tottfgpos.c LigCaretCnt/DumpLigCarets: non-zero carets, or all carets when the count is fixed; ascending, descending for RTL). babelfont stores LCarets2 as format_specific 'sfd.lcarets' and never turns it into Glyphs caret_N anchors, which fontbe get_ligature_carets would compile.
rows.evidence: The prototype adds caret_N anchors: 15 LigGlyphs, equal to the release (runs/p2-proto). probes/lcarets_census.py: Cardo-Italic is the only style in either batch with exportable carets, and its release has 15.

rows.cause: Same as Cardo-Regular: FontForge 2011-02-22 wrote 0 for a font with both LTR and RTL characters. fontc writes 2. The field is deprecated.
rows.evidence: runs/dirhint_oracle.txt: Cardo-Italic 0 0 MATCH bit9=1. The proposed gate reclassifies it (runs/p2-proto/Cardo-Italic.proposed.txt).

rows.row: GDEF.mark_glyph_sets [null, {0:[uni1DC1 ... uni05B105BD]}] and 'GDEF.glyph_classes -- a lookup filters on glyph class' (appear once advancing marks keep their width)
rows.cause: The release's kern lookup has flag 0, from the .sfd `Lookup: 258 0 0`. fontc's kern writer (ufo2ft KernFeatureWriter semantics) always ignores marks. When some marks advance, it uses UseMarkFilteringSet over those marks, which adds the MarkGlyphSetsDef and a class-reading flag. fontir 1.0.0 feature_writers.rs:197-200 turns ufo2ft's ignoreMarks=false into a hard error, although fontbe kern.rs:1130 already has the ignore_marks=false path. The same gap exists at r0 (kern flag 8 vs 0), where the gate hid it.
rows.evidence: runs/p2-proto: shared 3 rows, proposed 2. probes/simulate_kern_flag0.py clears bits 0x8/0x10 and the filtering set on the kern-writer lookups of the p2 build, then re-runs d3 and both gates: shared 1, proposed 0 (runs/p2-sim-kernflag0). This is a SIMULATION, not a build.

rows.row: kern across a combining mark: 2056 of 3057 kerned pairs with U+0301/U+0308/U+0323 between (not a gate row)
rows.cause: The release's flag-0 kern lookup lets an intervening mark block the pair; our IgnoreMarks lookup kerns across it. The gate accepts any GPOS difference when both fonts have lookups.
rows.evidence: probes/shaping_compare.py corpus kern+mark: r0, s1 and p2 all show 2056/3057; the p2 build with simulated flag-0 kern shows 0/3057 (runs/shaping_summary.txt).

rows.cause: Same rule: FontForge 2011-02-22, the release maps Hebrew and Latin, so 0. fontc writes 2. The field is deprecated.
rows.evidence: runs/dirhint_oracle.txt Cardo-Bold 0 0 MATCH bit9=1. runs/s1-bold-workarounds: shared 1 row, proposed 0.

rows.cause: fontc 1.0.0 ignores a single-master Glyphs source's instance weightClass (issues/fontc-static-weight-class.md). The .sfd states TTFWeight: 700. tools/land.py closes it inside the convert commit with tools/workarounds.py (weight-class as FEA). baseline.sh measures the converter alone, so the row always appears there. The unit brief said Bold had only head.font_direction_hint; baseline-next.tsv shows both rows.
rows.evidence: Run through next-fstype/probes/bf_with_workarounds.sh (WORKAROUNDS=1 in probes/run_stage.sh), runs/s1-bold-workarounds goes from 2 shared rows to 1.

rows.row: kern across a combining mark: 177 of 426 kerned pairs (not a gate row)
rows.cause: The release kern lookup has flag 0, and the release also classes U+0300.. as base (the gate discloses the 163 GDEF mark classes as a correction). Our kern writer lookups have IgnoreMarks, so 'B + U+0301 + A' kerns in ours (B 1379) and not in the release (B 1482).
rows.evidence: runs/shaping_summary.txt: s1 and p2 show 177/426, and the simulated flag-0 kern shows 0/426 (runs/p2-sim-kernflag0/Cardo-Bold.shaping.txt).

proposed_sfd_edits.commit_subject: Rename glyph 10192.04 to u10192.04 in Cardo-Regular-TTF.sfd
proposed_sfd_edits.commit_body:
A feature file cannot name a glyph that starts with a digit (OpenType
Feature File spec 2.f.i), so the salt rules of u10192 and u10198 that
list it could not be compiled. The new name follows the glyph's
siblings u10192.03 and u10198.01-.05. Only the post name of U+F438
changes; outline, advance and mappings are unchanged.
proposed_sfd_edits.value_derived_from: The source's own naming of the other salt alternates of U+10192 and U+10198 (u10192.03, u10198.01, u10198.03-.05). The release keeps the name 10192.04, because FontForge wrote the .sfd name into post format 2. The gate reports the rename as ACCEPTED-RENAME cmap U+F438 (same outline and advance).
proposed_sfd_edits.source_currently_states: StartChar: 10192.04 / Encoding: 62520 62520 3416 / Width: 1088 / GlyphClass: 2, referenced in two AlternateSubs2 lines of "'salt' Stylistic Alternatives in Latin lookup 24 subtable" (glyphs u10192 and u10198)

proposed_sfd_edits.commit_subject: Give nonbreakingspace the space's width in Cardo-Italic-TTF.sfd
proposed_sfd_edits.commit_body:
google/fonts d70318ab8 (2015-04-27, "Updating ofl/cardo/*ttf with
nbspace and fsType fixes") set the shipped Cardo-Italic's
nonbreakingspace advance from 550 to 575, the space's width. It changed
nothing else in the font. The source now states what Google Fonts ships.
proposed_sfd_edits.value_derived_from: google/fonts d70318ab8 edited the binary. probes/cardo_release_history.py shows the only advance change from 90abd17b4 to d70318ab8 is nonbreakingspace 550->575, and 575 is the .sfd's space Width.

proposed_tool_changes.description: Write the feature-writer insertion marker as '# Automatic Code' (ufo2ft INSERT_FEATURE_MARKER spelling) instead of '# Automatic code start' in convertors/fontforge.rs (the abvm/blwm/kern/dist/mark/mkmk blocks). With the current spelling fontc and ufo2ft treat those features as hand-written and generate no mark/mkmk/abvm/blwm lookups from the converted anchors. babelfont's own subsetlayout.rs already tests for '# Automatic Code'.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: fea-rs 1.0.0 typed.rs has_insert_marker uses starts_with("# Automatic Code"). The fontc warning 'Skipping generating feature mark' is reproduced. Cardo-Regular: base+mark shaping differences 4361 -> 956 of 181328. probes/automatic_code_marker.py: in the next batch it affects Cardo-Regular (mark) and Lohit-Bengali (abvm); no landed repository (kern is exempt because glyphs-reader appends the marker to a manual kern feature). Regression check: Italiana, Sanchez x2, Lohit-Bengali and Lohit-Tamil keep their gate verdicts and shaping counts (runs/reg-proto).

proposed_tool_changes.description: FontForge reader: turn LCarets2 into Glyphs caret_1..caret_n anchors (x = caret, y = 0) on every foreground layer, following FontForge's GDEF writer: non-zero carets only unless LigCaretCntFixed is set, ascending, or descending for a right-to-left glyph. Also parse LigCaretCntFixed.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: Cardo-Italic GDEF.lig_carets row closes: 15 LigGlyphs equal to the release (runs/p2-proto). FontForge v20110222 tottfgpos.c LigCaretCnt/DumpLigCarets and sfd.c LigCaretCntFixed. probes/lcarets_census.py: Cardo-Italic is the only style in either batch with exportable carets.
proposed_tool_changes.prototype: same patch: lig_carets() and the glyph-finalization block in convertors/fontforge.rs

proposed_tool_changes.description: An advancing mark is 'Spacing Combining', not 'Nonspacing'. The SFD reader (GlyphClass 4 with a non-zero Width) and the --set-subcategory filter (a mark with an _anchor and a non-zero advance in any layer) both set it. A Glyphs compiler exports a Nonspacing mark zero-width (glyphs2fontir 1.0.0 source.rs:1828); a SpacingCombining mark keeps its advance and stays GDEF class 3. The reader half is the next-provenance unit's babelfont-spacing-combining-mark.patch; the set-subcategory half is new here, because that filter overwrote the reader's value for marks with anchors (Cardo-Regular uni0304 and uni05B105BD).
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: Italic: 6 hmtx rows close (2 of them hidden by the gate). Regular: 2 hidden rows close. Lohit-Tamil u0BC1 and u0BC2 close (runs/reg-proto: 8 -> 6 rows). 0 advance differences in all three Cardo p2 builds. Side effect: fontc's kern writer then uses a mark filtering set over these marks (Italic GDEF.mark_glyph_sets row); see the fontc change below.
proposed_tool_changes.prototype: same patch: convertors/fontforge.rs glyph finalization and filters/setsubcategory.rs
proposed_tool_changes.upstream_pr_needed: babelfont-rs (simoncozens): one PR, or fold it into the next-provenance unit's PR.

proposed_tool_changes.description: Keep FontForge's lookup precedence around compiler-generated lookups. For a feature that carries the insertion marker, define the lookups that only this feature references after the marker, inside the feature block, rather than in featurePrefixes. fea-rs then inserts the generated mark-to-base lookups before them (InsertionPoint = next_gpos_id() at the marker) instead of after every lookup the file defines. A lookup used by another feature or by a contextual lookup stays in the prefix.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: Cardo-Regular with every other fix still differs in 10 base+mark strings and 7 diffenator3 words (Hebrew cantillation over vowels). probes/lookup_order_test.py shows the order is the whole cause, and that the release's MarkBasePos lookups placed first shape identically to the release (0/241128). probes/mark_lookups_after_marker.py applies this layout to the converted .glyphs, and a real builder3 e851b8b / fontc 1.0.0 build of it gives 0 differences in every corpus and proposed gate 0 (runs/p3-marks-first). This is EMULATED on the .glyphs, not implemented in Rust. The general case (FontForge interleaving that marks-first does not reproduce) would need explicit FEA mark lookups in .sfd order.
proposed_tool_changes.upstream_pr_needed: babelfont-rs (simoncozens): design change to discuss with Simon before a PR.

proposed_tool_changes.description: Honour ufo2ft's KernFeatureWriter option ignoreMarks=false (featureWriters userData) instead of rejecting it as unsupported. fontbe already has the path (KernSplitOptions.ignore_marks / make_lookups). Companion babelfont change: when a FontForge source's kern lookups carry no IgnoreMarks flag, write that featureWriters option into the Glyphs userData, so the kern lookup keeps FontForge's flag 0 and gets no spacing-mark filtering set.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: fontir 1.0.0 feature_writers.rs:197-200 hard-errors on 'KernFeatureWriter ignoreMarks=false'; fontbe kern.rs:1130 has the branch. Simulated with probes/simulate_kern_flag0.py on the p2 builds: Italic shared 3 -> 1 and proposed 2 -> 0 rows; kern+mark shaping Italic 2056/3057 -> 0 and Bold 177/426 -> 0. probes/kern_scan.sh (runs/kern_scan.tsv) finds kern-across-mark differences in 5 of the 126 builds kept in scratch: Cardo-Bold, Cardo-Italic, Salsa-Regular (246/285, landed CLEAN), Poly-Regular (2), Varela-Regular (4).
proposed_tool_changes.prototype: /home/fsanches/compartilhado/sfd-reland/investigations/next-cardo/probes/simulate_kern_flag0.py (simulation on built fonts; no fontc build)
proposed_tool_changes.upstream_pr_needed: fontc (googlefonts/fontc): feature parity with ufo2ft, needs an issue or PR; then babelfont-rs for the userData entry. Felipe files both.

proposed_tool_changes.description: Recipe fidelity flag --fontforge-no-anchor-propagation (the Glyphs custom parameter 'Propagate Anchors' = 0): FontForge exports only a glyph's own anchors. The filter is the next-provenance unit's prototype, applied unchanged; it has to be registered in filters/mod.rs and passed by tools/recipe.py for FontForge sources.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: Cardo-Regular p1 -> p2 (the only change is this flag): base+mark shaping differences 956 -> 10 of 181328 (runs/shaping_summary.txt).
proposed_tool_changes.upstream_pr_needed: babelfont-rs (simoncozens): owned by the next-provenance proposal.

proposed_tool_changes.description: (a) Never hide an advance: expand_overflow also recomputes advances when diffenator3 overflows the hmtx section, and arbitrate_lsb keeps the width part of a row BLOCKING. (b) Arbitrate head.font_direction_hint as RELEASE-STALE when the release value is not 2, ours is 2, the release has FFTM stamped before FontForge 722e7ea8873e (2017-12-23), and the value and head.flags bit 9 are what that exporter computed from the release's own cmap. (c) Replace the structural GPOS acceptance ('legacy kern modernised') with a shaping test such as probes/shaping_compare.py, comparing absolute glyph positions: it passed a build that had lost every mark-to-base lookup.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: (a) probes/advance_audit.py found hidden widths in Cardo-Italic (2), Cardo-Regular (2) and Lohit-Tamil (5). (b) The oracle matches 147 of 149 releases (misses: Tuffy x2, which have no FFTM). (c) runs/kern_scan.tsv shows letter-pair kerning differences the gate passed in Italiana-Regular (726/13689, landed CLEAN: FontForge's one lookup holds the same pair in two subtables, e.g. B v -20, and babelfont emitted an FEA lookup plus Glyphs kerning, so ours kerns twice, B 530 against 550), Ultra-Regular (260) and Thabit x2, and Cardo-Regular r1 passed with 4361 base+mark differences. Sweep over the 106 next builds: only Cardo-Italic 10->11, Cardo-Bold 2->1 and Lohit-Tamil 8->13 change verdict; no CLEAN style becomes BLOCKING (runs/proposed_gate_sweep.tsv). First-batch builds: Kristi-Regular 0->1 and NosiferCaps-Regular 1->2, both from a .notdef advance of 748 vs 1024 (runs/proposed_gate_sweep_first.tsv).

proposed_tool_changes.description: Diagnostics only, no output change for valid sources. babelfont should refuse or warn, naming the glyph, when a glyph that converted FEA references has a name FEA cannot express (a leading digit), instead of writing FEA that no compiler accepts. gftools-builder3 should print fontc's fea-rs diagnostics; it now reports only 'FEA parsing failed with 2 errors', even with -v.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: Cardo-Regular 10192.04. Repro: probes/fea_digit_glyphname (fontc 1.0.0 and feaLib both reject). builder3 e851b8b -v prints only the count; the fontc CLI prints the location and token.

decisions_for_felipe: Where to land Cardo. googlefonts/CardoFont is ARCHIVED on GitHub (read-only; archived: true, last push 2021-03-01, 2 forks, open issue #1 from 2017 'Glyph differences amongst Italic and Roman' that its author chose to ignore). Its main (fc675d7, identical on GitHub and in the repo archive) is 3 commits past the recorded b2bf876, all by Marc Foley on 2017-06-09: 'converd .sfd to .glyphs', 'updated metadata to match gf spec', 'fonts now compile'. They add an unshipped Glyphs 2 conversion (appVersion 1032): sources/Cardo.glyphs with 2 masters (Regular + Bold, version 1.500, 3844 glyphs, 10192.04 dropped, 576 glyphs lacking a layer) and sources/Cardo-Italic.glyphs (2388 glyphs). There is no config.yaml and no fonts, and nothing was built or shipped from them. land.py (kind upstream) would branch modernize-sfd-to-glyphs from b2bf876, diverging from main. A googlefonts admin must unarchive the repository before any push; otherwise use another repository. You also decide what happens to Marc's .glyphs on main.
The new name for glyph 10192.04 (proposed u10192.04, after its siblings). Only U+F438's post name changes.

Adopt the gate changes: advance widths can no longer be hidden, and head.font_direction_hint is arbitrated for pre-2019 FontForge exports. Decide whether a .notdef advance counts: the change newly blocks landed Kristi-Regular and NosiferCaps-Regular (.notdef 748 vs 1024). Tuffy's plan already made an .notdef edit.

Replace the gate's structural GPOS acceptance with a shaping test. That would reopen landed repositories the current gate passed: Italiana-Regular kerns 726 of 13689 letter pairs twice (-40 against -20), and Salsa-Regular kerns across marks in 246 of 285 cases. Ultra-Regular (260 pairs) needs its own unit.
